## Why Choose HK?

### Shipshape

Rust-native startup and parallel execution keep every hook fast

### Batten Down the Hatches

Secures staged changes while keeping unstaged work safe in port

### Tackle Box

A well-stocked collection of pre-rigged linters and formatters

### Captain's Log

Type-safe Pkl configuration catches mistakes before hooks run

### First Mate

mise integration keeps project tools and tasks reproducible

### All Hands on Deck

Smart file locking lets your whole crew work simultaneously

# fcitx5-vinput **Voice input for Fcitx5 — local and cloud ASR, LLM rewriting, cross-distro packages** [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput)](LICENSE) [![CI](https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/actions/workflows/release.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput)](https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/releases) [![AUR](https://img.shields.io/aur/version/fcitx5-vinput-bin)](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/fcitx5-vinput-bin) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/total)](https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/releases) [English](README.md) | [中文](README_zh.md) | [Documentation](https://xifan2333.github.io/fcitx5-vinput/) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a548a68-153c-4842-bab6-926f30bb720e
## Features - **Two trigger modes** — tap to toggle recording, or hold to push-to-talk - **Local & cloud ASR** — offline [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) models or cloud providers (Doubao, Aliyun Bailian, ElevenLabs, OpenAI-compatible), switchable at runtime with `F8` - **LLM post-processing** — error correction, formatting, translation via scenes - **Command mode** — select text, speak an instruction, release to apply - **GUI & CLI** — `vinput-gui` for quick setup, `vinput` CLI for full control - **Cross-distro** — Arch, Fedora, Ubuntu/Debian, Nix, Flatpak ## Installation ### Arch Linux ([archlinuxcn](https://www.archlinuxcn.org/archlinux-cn-repo-and-mirror/) / AUR) If you use the [archlinuxcn](https://www.archlinuxcn.org/archlinux-cn-repo-and-mirror/) repository, install the repo-built package: ```bash sudo pacman -S fcitx5-vinput ``` The AUR binary package is also available: ```bash yay -S fcitx5-vinput-bin ``` ### Fedora (COPR) ```bash sudo dnf copr enable xifan/fcitx5-vinput-bin sudo dnf install fcitx5-vinput ``` ### Ubuntu 24.04 (PPA) ```bash sudo add-apt-repository ppa:xifan233/ppa sudo apt update sudo apt install fcitx5-vinput ``` ### Ubuntu / Debian (manual) ```bash # Download latest .deb from GitHub Releases sudo dpkg -i fcitx5-vinput_*.deb sudo apt-get install -f ``` ### Nix (flake) Supports `x86_64-linux` and `aarch64-linux`. ```nix inputs.fcitx5-vinput.url = "github:xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput"; ``` Binary cache via [Cachix](https://fcitx5-vinput.cachix.org): ```nix nixConfig = { extra-substituters = [ "https://fcitx5-vinput.cachix.org" ]; extra-trusted-public-keys = [ "fcitx5-vinput.cachix.org-1:XpX3AA6+dDIX4qJhb1QM7sbTwX6/qSlGvW8Z5NK6XdU=" ];

[tools]
pandoc = "latest"
node = "22"

[env]
_.file = ".env"

[tasks.default]
description = "List available tasks"
run = "mise tasks"

[tasks.fmt]
description = "Format C++ source code with clang-format"
run = "find src tests -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.h' | xargs clang-format -i"

[tasks.check-fmt]
description = "Check C++ source formatting without modifying files"
run = "find src tests -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.h' | xargs clang-format --dry-run --Werror"

[tasks.check-i18n]
description = "Validate gettext and Qt translation files"
run = "python3 scripts/check-i18n.py"

[tasks.lint]
description = "Run linter and check i18n & JSON formatting"
depends = ["check-fmt", "check-i18n"]
run = """
python3 -m json.tool data/default-config.json >/dev/null
python3 -m json.tool notification.json >/dev/null
"""

[tasks.gen-man]
description = "Generate roff man pages from markdown using pandoc"
run = "bash scripts/gen-man.sh"

[tasks.tidy]
description = "Run clang-tidy on C++ source files"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
if [ ! -f "build/compile_commands.json" ]; then
  echo "compile_commands.json not found in build. Run 'mise run configure' first." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
  clang-tidy -p build "$1"
else
  if command -v run-clang-tidy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    run-clang-tidy -p build -header-filter='src/.*' 'src/.*'
  else
    find src -name '*.cpp' | xargs -n 1 -P $(nproc) clang-tidy -p build
  fi
fi
"""

[tasks.configure]
description = "Configure CMake build directory (Release by default, or: mise run configure Debug /usr)"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
type="${1:-Release}"
prefix="${2:-/usr}"
shift 2 2>/dev/null || shift 1 2>/dev/null || true
if [ "$type" = "Debug" ]; then
  cmake --preset debug-clang-mold -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$prefix" "$@"
else
  cmake --preset release-clang-mold -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$prefix" "$@"
fi
"""

[tasks.dev]
description = "Configure CMake for debug build"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
prefix="${1:-/usr}"
shift 1 2>/dev/null || true
cmake --preset debug-clang-mold -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$prefix" "$@"
"""

[tasks.configure-release]
description = "Configure CMake for release build"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
prefix="${1:-/usr}"
shift 1 2>/dev/null || true
cmake --preset release-clang-mold -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$prefix" "$@"
"""

[tasks.build]
description = "Build project with CMake (Release preset)"
run = "cmake --build --preset release-clang-mold"

[tasks.build-debug]
description = "Build project with CMake (Debug preset)"

[tasks.clean]
description = "Remove CMake build directory"
run = "rm -rf build"

[tasks.rebuild]
description = "Clean and rebuild the project (default Release /usr)"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
rm -rf build
type="${1:-Release}"
prefix="${2:-/usr}"
shift 2 2>/dev/null || shift 1 2>/dev/null || true
if [ "$type" = "Debug" ]; then
  cmake --preset debug-clang-mold -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$prefix" "$@"

[tasks.install]
description = "Install built binaries, systemd units and man pages"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
prefix="${1:-/usr}"
cmake --preset release-clang-mold -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$prefix"
cmake --install build
echo "note: run 'systemctl --user daemon-reload' after installing systemd user units"
if [ "$prefix" = "/usr" ]; then

fi

description = "Run full system diagnostic checks"
depends = ["check-build-cache", "check-installed-binaries", "check-user-service", "check-stale-install"]

[tasks.check-build-cache]
description = "Inspect CMake build cache"
run = """
echo "== Build Cache =="
cmake -LA -N build 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE|CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX' || true
echo
"""

[tasks.check-installed-binaries]
description = "Check installed vinput executable paths"
run = """
echo "== Installed Binaries =="
for cmd in vinput vinput-daemon vinput-gui; do
  if command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    path="$(command -v "$cmd")"
    echo "$cmd -> $path"
    ls -l "$path"
  else
    echo "$cmd -> (not found)"
  fi
  echo
done
"""

[tasks.check-user-service]
description = "Check systemd user service status"
run = """
echo "== User Service =="
systemctl --user cat vinput-daemon.service || true
echo
"""

[tasks.check-stale-install]
description = "Check for conflicting /usr/local legacy paths"
run = """
echo "== Stale /usr/local Paths =="
found=0
for p in /usr/local/bin/vinput /usr/local/bin/vinput-daemon /usr/local/bin/vinput-gui \
         /usr/local/share/systemd/user/vinput-daemon.service \
         /usr/local/share/dbus-1/services/org.fcitx.Vinput.service \
         /usr/local/share/applications/vinput-gui.desktop; do
  if [ -e "$p" ]; then
    found=1
    ls -ld "$p"
  fi
done
[ "$found" -eq 0 ] && echo "(none)" || true
echo
"""

run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
version_value="${1:-}"
ref="${2:-main}"
if [ -z "${version_value}" ]; then
  version_value="$(tr -d '\n' < VERSION)"
fi
git tag "v${version_value}" "${ref}"
git push origin "v${version_value}"
"""

description = "Trigger GitHub Actions packaging channels workflow"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ref="${1:-main}"
version_value="${2:-}"
ppa_revision_value="${3:-}"
if [ -z "${version_value}" ]; then
  version_value="$(tr -d '\n' < VERSION)"
fi
extra_fields=()
if [ -n "${ppa_revision_value}" ]; then
  extra_fields+=(--field ppa_revision="${ppa_revision_value}")
fi
gh workflow run channels.yml \
  --ref main \
  --field ref="${ref}" \
  --field version="${version_value}" \
  "${extra_fields[@]}"
"""

# Contributing

Thanks for your interest in fcitx5-vinput!

## Documentation

Full documentation is available at the [project site](https://xifan2333.github.io/fcitx5-vinput/). For registry contribution guidelines (ASR providers, LLM adapters, models), see the [Registry](https://xifan2333.github.io/fcitx5-vinput/registry/) page.

## Build from Source

**Dependencies:** cmake, fcitx5, pipewire, libcurl, nlohmann-json, CLI11, Qt6

```bash
sudo bash scripts/build-sherpa-onnx.sh
cmake --preset release-clang-mold
cmake --build --preset release-clang-mold
sudo cmake --install build
```

Or use `mise`:

```bash
mise run sherpa
mise run configure-release
mise run build
sudo mise run install
```

## Project Structure

- `src/addon/` — Fcitx5 addon (key events, D-Bus client, UI)
- `src/daemon/` — ASR daemon (audio capture, inference, post-processing)
- `src/common/` — Shared code (configs, D-Bus interface, scenes)
- `src/cli/` — `vinput` CLI tool
- `site/` — Documentation site (Astro + Starlight)

## Submitting Changes

1. Fork the repo and create a branch from `main`
2. Make your changes — keep commits focused and atomic
3. Test locally: enable the addon in Fcitx5, verify the daemon works
4. Open a PR with a clear description of what and why

## Reporting Bugs

Use the [Bug Report](https://github.com/xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) template. Include:
- Version (`vinput --version`)
- Distribution
- Daemon logs: `journalctl --user -u vinput-daemon.service`

## Contributing to the Registry

The [vinput-registry](https://github.com/xifan2333/vinput-registry) repository hosts downloadable resources: ASR models, cloud ASR provider scripts, and LLM adapter scripts.

To contribute a new provider, adapter, or model, see the [Registry](https://xifan2333.github.io/fcitx5-vinput/registry/) page for the full specification.

Key rules:
- Scripts must be self-contained — standard library only, no third-party dependencies
- Python 3 is recommended; other runtimes are acceptable
- Each script resource needs an `entry.py` (or equivalent) and `README.md`
- Add i18n entries for both `en_US.json` and `zh_CN.json`

## Translations

Translation files are in `po/`. To add a new language:

1. Copy `po/fcitx5-vinput.pot` to `po/<lang>.po`
2. Fill in the translations
3. Submit a PR

## Code Style

- C++20
- Follow the existing style in the codebase

### General Prettier Formatting

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/builtins.html

Uses Prettier to enforce consistent code style across a wide range of file types including web assets, configs, and documentation.

```bash
prettier --check {{ files }}
prettier --write {{ files }}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure commit-msg hook to validate commit message format

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/hooks.html

This PKL configuration sets up the 'commit-msg' hook. It includes a 'validate-commit-msg' step that uses 'grep' to check if the commit message starts with a valid prefix (e.g., 'fix:', 'feat:', 'chore:'). If the format is invalid, the command exits with a status code of 1, failing the commit.

```pkl
hooks {
    ["commit-msg"] {
        steps {
            ["validate-commit-msg"] {
                check = "grep -q '^(fix|feat|chore):' {{commit_msg_file}} || exit 1"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Hooks > `commit-msg`

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/hooks.html

Runs when `git commit` is run after the commit message is created. Useful for validating the commit message against certain conventions, such as ensuring it starts with a valid type prefix like 'fix', 'feat', or 'chore'.

--------------------------------

### Hooks > `pre-commit`

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/hooks.html

Runs when `git commit` is run before `git commit` creates the commit. This hook is useful for running code formatters and linters to ensure code quality before a commit is finalized.

--------------------------------

### hk documentation > <STEP>.stdin: String

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/configuration.html

If set, sends the template-expanded string to the command's stdin (mutually exclusive with `interactive`). Supports variable `file_list` (`list[str]`) and Tera builtins.
This is useful for tools which allow passing filenames via stdin (like xargs), to avoid hk's automatic batching.

# Built-in Linters Reference [​](#built-in-linters-reference)

hk provides 150+ pre-configured linters and formatters through the `Builtins` module. Each builtin supplies the command, file matching, batching, and other hk behavior; the corresponding tool must be available in the step's environment.

## Usage [​](#usage)

Import and use builtins in your `hk.pkl`:

pkl
```
amends "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.57.0/hk@1.57.0#/Config.pkl"
import "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.57.0/hk@1.57.0#/Builtins.pkl"

hooks {
  ["pre-commit"] {
    steps {
      ["prettier"] = Builtins.prettier
      ["eslint"] = Builtins.eslint
    }
  }
}
```

You can also customize builtins:

pkl
```
["prettier"] = (Builtins.prettier) {
  batch = false  // Override the default batch setting
  glob = List("*.js", "*.ts")  // Override file patterns
}
```

### Tool availability [​](#tool-availability)

Builtins configure how hk invokes a tool; they do not install that tool. The executable used by the builtin must be on `PATH`, or the step must use a `prefix` that resolves it.

With [`HK_MISE=1`](https://hk.jdx.dev/mise_integration.html#per-directory-environments-monorepos), hk resolves the mise environment for the step's directory, so tools declared in a subproject's `mise.toml` are available without a prefix. For a Node tool installed locally by aube, prefix its builtin with `aube exec`:

pkl
```
["eslint"] = (Builtins.eslint) {
  prefix = List("aube", "exec")
}
```

Use an argv list for builtins backed by structured commands. A string prefix such as `"aube exec"` or `"mise x --"` cannot be combined with those commands.

The generated list below summarizes each builtin. The complete command and defaults for each builtin are defined in the corresponding Pkl file in [`pkl/builtins`](https://github.com/jdx/hk/tree/main/pkl/builtins).

## Customizing Builtins [​](#customizing-builtins)

### Override Properties [​](#override-properties)

pkl
```
["prettier"] = (Builtins.prettier) {
  // Override glob patterns
  glob = List("src/**/*.js", "src/**/*.ts")

  // Disable batch processing
  batch = false

  // Add environment variables
  env {
    ["PRETTIER_CONFIG"] = ".prettierrc.json"
  }
}
```

### Add Dependencies [​](#add-dependencies)

pkl
```
["eslint"] = (Builtins.eslint) {
  // Run after prettier
  depends = "prettier"
}
```

### Workspace-Specific Configuration [​](#workspace-specific-configuration)

pkl
```
["cargo_clippy"] = (Builtins.cargo_clippy) {
  // Only run in directories with Cargo.toml
  workspace_indicator = "Cargo.toml"

  // Custom command using workspace
  check = "cargo clippy --manifest-path {{workspace}}/Cargo.toml"
}
```

### Profile-Based Configuration [​](#profile-based-configuration)

pkl
```
["mypy"] = (Builtins.mypy) {
  // Only run with "python" profile
  profiles = List("python")
}
```

## Creating Custom Steps [​](#creating-custom-steps)

If a builtin doesn't exist for your tool:

pkl
```
["custom-tool"] {
  glob = List("*.custom")
  check = "custom-tool --check {{files}}"
  fix = "custom-tool --fix {{files}}"
  batch = true  // Enable parallel processing
}
```

# Built-in Linters Reference [​](#built-in-linters-reference)

hk provides 150+ pre-configured linters and formatters through the `Builtins` module. Each builtin supplies the command, file matching, batching, and other hk behavior; the corresponding tool must be available in the step's environment.

## Usage [​](#usage)

Import and use builtins in your `hk.pkl`:

pkl
```
amends "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.57.0/hk@1.57.0#/Config.pkl"
import "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.57.0/hk@1.57.0#/Builtins.pkl"

hooks {
  ["pre-commit"] {
    steps {
      ["prettier"] = Builtins.prettier
      ["eslint"] = Builtins.eslint
    }
  }
}
```

You can also customize builtins:

pkl
```
["prettier"] = (Builtins.prettier) {
  batch = false  // Override the default batch setting
  glob = List("*.js", "*.ts")  // Override file patterns
}
```

### Tool availability [​](#tool-availability)

Builtins configure how hk invokes a tool; they do not install that tool. The executable used by the builtin must be on `PATH`, or the step must use a `prefix` that resolves it.

With [`HK_MISE=1`](https://hk.jdx.dev/mise_integration.html#per-directory-environments-monorepos), hk resolves the mise environment for the step's directory, so tools declared in a subproject's `mise.toml` are available without a prefix. For a Node tool installed locally by aube, prefix its builtin with `aube exec`:

pkl
```
["eslint"] = (Builtins.eslint) {
  prefix = List("aube", "exec")
}
```

Use an argv list for builtins backed by structured commands. A string prefix such as `"aube exec"` or `"mise x --"` cannot be combined with those commands.

The generated list below summarizes each builtin. The complete command and defaults for each builtin are defined in the corresponding Pkl file in [`pkl/builtins`](https://github.com/jdx/hk/tree/main/pkl/builtins).

通过查阅 [hk 官方文档](https://hk.jdx.dev/) 与 Context7 中的技术文档，以下是关于 **hk** 的核心特性解析以及**如何为 `fcitx5-vinput` 项目接入 hk** 的完整落地指南：

---

### 一、什么是 hk？

**hk** 是由 `mise` 作者（jdx）用 Rust 编写的高性能现代化 Git Hook 管理器，专为解决传统 pre-commit 工具速度慢、不支持并发或并发时文件竞争冲突等痛点而设计：

1. **并行执行与智能文件锁（File Locking）**：多个 formatter/linter 并行执行，并通过文件级锁机制保证修改同一文件时不会发生写冲突。
2. **Smart Stash（安全暂存）**：仅暂存工作区未 stage 的修改，hook 和 fixer 严格仅作用于本次要 commit 的暂存代码，避免污染工作区半成品。
3. **原生深度集成 `mise`**：与 `mise` 配合无缝解析环境变量、工具链路与 task。
4. **类型安全配置（Pkl）**：采用 Apple 的 Pkl 语言编写 `hk.pkl`，内置 150+ 种常用工具（如 `clang-format`、`mise`、`jq`、`trailing-whitespace` 等）。

---

### 二、针对 `fcitx5-vinput` 的接入方案

当前 `fcitx5-vinput` 的开发流中：
- 已经使用 **`mise`** 管理开发环境与任务（`mise.toml`）。
- 拥有 C++ 源码（`.clang-format` / `.clang-tidy`）、i18n 脚本（`scripts/check-i18n.py`）、JSON 配置文件（`data/default-config.json` 等）。
- CI 中配置了 `cpp-linter.yml` 进行格式检查。

接入 `hk` 后，可以在本地 `git commit` 时**秒级自动格式化 C++ 代码、检查 i18n / JSON 正确性、拦截冲突标记与私钥泄露**，彻底避免因为格式问题导致 CI 失败。

---

### 三、具体落地步骤

#### 1. 在 `mise.toml` 中添加 `hk` 和 `pkl` 工具

在项目根目录的 `mise.toml` 的 `[tools]` 区域添加 `hk` 与 `pkl`：

```toml
[tools]
pandoc = "latest"
node = "22"
hk = "latest"
pkl = "latest"
```

并在 `mise.toml` 的 `[tasks]` 中添加便捷任务：

```toml
[tasks.hooks-install]
description = "Install hk git hooks with mise integration"
run = "hk install --mise"

[tasks.check]
description = "Run all hk checks across the repo"
run = "hk check"

[tasks.fix]
description = "Run all hk fixers to format files"
run = "hk fix"
```

---

#### 2. 创建 `hk.pkl` 配置文件

在项目根目录下新建 `hk.pkl`，配置契合本项目的 linters 和 hooks：

```pkl
amends "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.57.0/hk@1.57.0#/Config.pkl"
import "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.57.0/hk@1.57.0#/Builtins.pkl"

// 定义项目专用的代码检查与格式化工具集
local linters = new Mapping<String, Step> {
  // 1. C++ 格式化（自动读取项目下的 .clang-format）
  ["clang-format"] = (Builtins["clang-format"]) {
    glob = List("src/**/*.cpp", "src/**/*.h", "tests/**/*.cpp", "tests/**/*.h")
  }

  // 2. mise.toml 格式化与检查
  ["mise"] = Builtins.mise

  // 3. i18n 多语言文件完整性校验
  ["check-i18n"] {
    glob = List("po/**", "src/**", "scripts/check-i18n.py")
    check = "python3 scripts/check-i18n.py"
  }

  // 4. JSON 配置文件语法校验
  ["json-validate"] {
    glob = List("data/default-config.json", "notification.json")
    check = "python3 -m json.tool {{files}} > /dev/null"
  }

  // 5. 基础文件卫生检查
  ["trailing-whitespace"] = Builtins["trailing-whitespace"]
  ["newlines"] = Builtins.newlines
  ["check-merge-conflict"] = Builtins["check-merge-conflict"]
  ["detect-private-key"] = Builtins["detect-private-key"]
}

// 注册 Git Hooks
hooks {
  // 提交前自动修复格式并校验
  ["pre-commit"] {
    fix = true
    stash = "patch-file"
    steps = linters
  }

  // Conventional Commit 规范校验（可选）
  ["commit-msg"] {
    steps {
      ["conventional-commit"] = Builtins["check-conventional-commit"]
    }
  }

  // 全量检查 (供 `hk check` 或 `mise run check` 调用)
  ["check"] {
    steps = linters
  }

  // 全量修复 (供 `hk fix` 或 `mise run fix` 调用)
  ["fix"] {
    fix = true
    steps = linters
  }
}
```

---

#### 3. 激活与验证

运行以下命令安装工具并注入 hooks：

```bash
# 1. 安装 mise 工具链 (包含 hk 和 pkl)
mise install

# 2. 安装 git hooks 并启用 mise 环境执行
hk install --mise

# 3. 本地运行一次全量检查验证配置
hk check
```

---

### 四、接入后的日常使用体验

- **常规开发提交**：直接正常执行 `git add . && git commit -m "feat: xxx"`。`hk` 会在 pre-commit 钩子中毫秒级并行执行 `clang-format` 修复、`check-i18n` 和 `json` 检查，并将修复结果自动写回暂存区。
- **全量手动检查**：执行 `mise run check` 或 `hk check`。
- **全量自动修复**：执行 `mise run fix` 或 `hk fix`。
OK， hk 的 agent 功能是什么

### Configure pre-commit hook with cargo-fmt and cargo-clippy

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/hooks.html

This snippet configures the 'pre-commit' hook using PKL. It includes steps for 'cargo-fmt' and 'cargo-clippy', both set to 'check_first = true' for safety. 'cargo-fmt' checks and formats Rust code, while 'cargo-clippy' checks and fixes Rust code with specific allowances for dirty and staged files.

```pkl
hooks {
    fix = true
    ["pre-commit"] {
        steps {
            ["cargo-fmt"] {
                glob = "*.rs"
                check_first = true
                check = "cargo fmt --check"
                fix = "cargo fmt"
            }
            ["cargo-clippy"] {
                glob = "*.rs"
                check_first = true
                check = "cargo clippy"
                fix = "cargo clippy --fix --allow-dirty --allow-staged"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

--------------------------------

### CLI Command: hk run

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/cli/run.html

Executes a hook with specified flags and subcommands to manage file processing, linting, or git hooks.

```APIDOC
## [CLI] hk run

### Description
Runs a hook based on the provided subcommand and flags. It supports running on specific files, glob patterns, or git-based references.

### Method
CLI Execution

### Endpoint
hk run [FLAGS] [FILES]… <SUBCOMMAND>

### Parameters
#### Arguments
- **[FILES]** (list) - Optional - Run on specific files.

#### Flags
- **-a, --all** (boolean) - Optional - Run on all files instead of just staged files.
- **-c, --check** (boolean) - Optional - Run check command instead of fix command.
- **-e, --exclude** (string) - Optional - Exclude files that otherwise would have been selected.
- **-f, --fix** (boolean) - Optional - Run fix command instead of check command.
- **-g, --glob** (string) - Optional - Run on files that match these glob patterns.
- **-P, --plan** (boolean) - Optional - Print the plan instead of running the hook.
- **-S, --step** (string) - Optional - Run only specific step(s).
- **--fail-fast** (boolean) - Optional - Abort on first failure.
- **--stash** (string) - Optional - Stash method to use (Choices: git, patch-file, none).

### Subcommands
- **commit-msg** - Run commit-msg hook.
- **pre-commit** - Run pre-commit hook.
- **pre-push** - Run pre-push hook.
- **prepare-commit-msg** - Run prepare-commit-msg hook.

### Request Example
hk run --fix --all pre-commit

### Response
#### Success Response (0)
- **stdout** (string) - Execution output and statistics.
```

--------------------------------

### Define hooks and linters in hk.pkl

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/getting_started

Example configuration file using Pkl to define linters like eslint and prettier, and hook stages like pre-commit.

```pkl
amends "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.38.0/hk@1.38.0#/Config.pkl"
import "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.38.0/hk@1.38.0#/Builtins.pkl"

local linters = new Mapping<String, Step> {
    ["eslint"] {
        glob = List("*.js", "*.ts")
        check = "eslint {{files}}"
    }
    ["prettier"] = Builtins.prettier
    ["prettier-yaml"] = (Builtins.prettier) {
        glob = List("*.yaml", "*.yml")
    }
}

hooks {
    ["pre-commit"] {
        fix = true
        stash = "git"
        steps {
            ["prelint"] {
                check = "mise run prelint"
                exclusive = true
            }
            ...linters
            ["postlint"] {
                check = "mise run postlint"
                exclusive = true
            }
        }
    }
}
```

--------------------------------

### `hk run pre-commit` Command

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/cli/run/pre-commit.html

Sets up git hooks to run hk on specified files or all files. Supports various flags for controlling the execution, such as checking, fixing, excluding, and staging.

```APIDOC
## `hk run pre-commit` Command

### Description
Sets up git hooks to run hk on specified files or all files. Supports various flags for controlling the execution, such as checking, fixing, excluding, and staging.

### Method
`RUN` (This is a command-line tool, not a typical HTTP method)

### Endpoint
`hk run pre-commit [FLAGS] [FILES]…`

### Arguments
#### `[FILES]…`
* **Type**: string array
* **Description**: Run on specific files.

### Flags
#### `-a, --all`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Run on all files instead of just staged files.

#### `-c, --check`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Run check command instead of fix command.

#### `-e, --exclude <EXCLUDE>`
* **Type**: string array
* **Description**: Exclude files that otherwise would have been selected.

#### `-f, --fix`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Run fix command instead of check command (this is the default behavior unless HK_FIX=0).

#### `-g, --glob <GLOB>`
* **Type**: string array
* **Description**: Run on files that match these glob patterns.

#### `-P, --plan`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Print the plan instead of running the hook.

#### `-S, --step <STEP>`
* **Type**: string array
* **Description**: Run only specific step(s).

#### `--fail-fast`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Abort on first failure.

#### `--from-ref <FROM_REF>`
* **Type**: string
* **Description**: Start reference for checking files (requires --to-ref).

#### `--no-fail-fast`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Continue on failures (opposite of --fail-fast).

#### `--no-stage`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Disable auto-staging of fixed files.

#### `--pr`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Check only files changed in the current PR/branch (shortcut for --from-ref DEFAULT_BRANCH --to-ref HEAD).

#### `--skip-step <STEP>`
* **Type**: string array
* **Description**: Skip specific step(s).

#### `--stage`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Enable auto-staging of fixed files.

#### `--stash <STASH>`
* **Type**: string
* **Description**: Stash method to use for git hooks.
* **Choices**: `git`, `patch-file`, `none`

#### `--stats`
* **Type**: boolean
* **Description**: Display statistics about files matching each step.

#### `--to-ref <TO_REF>`
* **Type**: string
* **Description**: End reference for checking files (requires --from-ref).

### Request Example
```bash
hk run pre-commit --all --fix
```

### Response
(This command typically provides output to the console indicating the status of the pre-commit hooks, rather than a structured JSON response.)

#### Success Response
(Output indicating successful execution of pre-commit hooks or no issues found.)

#### Response Example
```text
Running pre-commit hooks...
All checks passed.
```
```

### Getting Started > Usage

Source: https://hk.jdx.dev/getting_started

To enable hooks defined in the hk.pkl file, users must run the hk install command within the git repository. This command configures git to trigger the specified hooks, such as pre-commit or pre-push, during standard git operations. Once installed, git actions will automatically execute the defined linters and checks, ensuring consistent code quality throughout the development process.

# Coding agents [​](#coding-agents)

hk gives coding agents a narrow, inspectable way to run project checks and fixes. Agents can use structured CLI output everywhere, or the MCP server for persistent runs, cancellation, paged logs, diagnostics, diffs, and the interactive dashboard.

Generate a starting point without editing any host configuration:

sh
```
hk agent instructions --target codex
hk agent hooks --target claude-code
hk agent mcp --target vscode
```

Claude Desktop uses global host configuration and does not reliably launch servers from the project directory. Replace `/absolute/path/to/project` in its generated snippet before installing it.

Every generator writes only to stdout. Review the result and place or merge it into the appropriate host configuration yourself.

## Safe agent workflow [​](#safe-agent-workflow)

1. Inspect the project and request a plan.
2. Scope execution to changed files. Use `--files0-from` when exact filenames matter and `--cd` to choose the project root.
3. Inspect command effects and prefer safe execution. `--safe` rejects a run before any step starts if a runnable command is unknown or destructive.
4. Consume JSON or JSONL diagnostics and retain raw output when investigating parser warnings.
5. Review the resulting diff before accepting a fix.

Without MCP, a portable invocation is:

sh
```
{
  git diff --name-only -z
  git diff --cached --name-only -z
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z
} | hk run check --files0-from - --safe --format jsonl
```

## MCP [​](#mcp)

`hk mcp --root <project>` starts a STDIO MCP server. It does not listen on a network port. The root is fixed at startup (plus roots supplied by the host), and tools cannot introduce arbitrary filesystem paths or unrestricted shell commands.

Generate configuration for a supported host:

sh
```
hk agent mcp --target codex
hk agent mcp --target claude-desktop
hk agent mcp --target claude-code
hk agent mcp --target vscode
```

Codex, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and VS Code can use the structured MCP tools. Hosts that implement MCP Apps also receive the hk dashboard; other hosts receive the same structured content and a useful text fallback.

## Rich dashboard [​](#rich-dashboard)

The dashboard shows the current run, step status and timing, normalized diagnostics grouped by file, searchable logs, and the resulting diff. Mutating actions are limited to confirmed safe fixes, and the server remains the source of truth.

![hk MCP dashboard showing a completed project check](https://hk.jdx.dev/agent-dashboard.png)

*A completed project check in an MCP Apps host, with step timing and command effects.*

See the [dashboard demo runbook](https://hk.jdx.dev/agents/mcp-dashboard.html) for a deterministic project fixture.

## ChatGPT Desktop [​](#chatgpt-desktop)

ChatGPT Desktop can connect the local STDIO server through OpenAI's [Secure MCP Tunnel](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/secure-mcp-tunnels). Build hk, create the demo fixture, and initialize a local-STDIO tunnel whose MCP command is the absolute `hk mcp --root <fixture>` command. Run `tunnel-client doctor` before starting the tunnel, then create a development-mode app in ChatGPT and select the tunnel.

The tunnel is a development bridge. hk itself ships no HTTP listener, hosted service, or authentication system.

## Instructions and hooks [​](#instructions-and-hooks)

Use `hk agent instructions` for a concise block suitable for `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or a generic agent prompt. Use `hk agent hooks` for an optional Codex or Claude Code stop hook, or a VS Code task. Hook output is deliberately a snippet rather than an automatic installation: inspect its effect on your workflow before enabling it.

# Coding agents [​](#coding-agents)

hk gives coding agents a narrow, inspectable way to run project checks and fixes. Agents can use structured CLI output everywhere, or the MCP server for persistent runs, cancellation, paged logs, diagnostics, diffs, and the interactive dashboard.

Generate a starting point without editing any host configuration:

sh
```
hk agent instructions --target codex
hk agent hooks --target claude-code
hk agent mcp --target vscode
```

Claude Desktop uses global host configuration and does not reliably launch servers from the project directory. Replace `/absolute/path/to/project` in its generated snippet before installing it.

Every generator writes only to stdout. Review the result and place or merge it into the appropriate host configuration yourself.

## Safe agent workflow [​](#safe-agent-workflow)

1. Inspect the project and request a plan.
2. Scope execution to changed files. Use `--files0-from` when exact filenames matter and `--cd` to choose the project root.
3. Inspect command effects and prefer safe execution. `--safe` rejects a run before any step starts if a runnable command is unknown or destructive.
4. Consume JSON or JSONL diagnostics and retain raw output when investigating parser warnings.
5. Review the resulting diff before accepting a fix.

Without MCP, a portable invocation is:

sh
```
{
  git diff --name-only -z
  git diff --cached --name-only -z
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z
} | hk run check --files0-from - --safe --format jsonl
```

## MCP [​](#mcp)

`hk mcp --root <project>` starts a STDIO MCP server. It does not listen on a network port. The root is fixed at startup (plus roots supplied by the host), and tools cannot introduce arbitrary filesystem paths or unrestricted shell commands.

Generate configuration for a supported host:

sh
```
hk agent mcp --target codex
hk agent mcp --target claude-desktop
hk agent mcp --target claude-code
hk agent mcp --target vscode
```

Codex, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and VS Code can use the structured MCP tools. Hosts that implement MCP Apps also receive the hk dashboard; other hosts receive the same structured content and a useful text fallback.

## Rich dashboard [​](#rich-dashboard)

The dashboard shows the current run, step status and timing, normalized diagnostics grouped by file, searchable logs, and the resulting diff. Mutating actions are limited to confirmed safe fixes, and the server remains the source of truth.

![hk MCP dashboard showing a completed project check](https://hk.jdx.dev/agent-dashboard.png)

*A completed project check in an MCP Apps host, with step timing and command effects.*

See the [dashboard demo runbook](https://hk.jdx.dev/agents/mcp-dashboard.html) for a deterministic project fixture.

## ChatGPT Desktop [​](#chatgpt-desktop)

ChatGPT Desktop can connect the local STDIO server through OpenAI's [Secure MCP Tunnel](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/secure-mcp-tunnels). Build hk, create the demo fixture, and initialize a local-STDIO tunnel whose MCP command is the absolute `hk mcp --root <fixture>` command. Run `tunnel-client doctor` before starting the tunnel, then create a development-mode app in ChatGPT and select the tunnel.

The tunnel is a development bridge. hk itself ships no HTTP listener, hosted service, or authentication system.

## Instructions and hooks [​](#instructions-and-hooks)

Use `hk agent instructions` for a concise block suitable for `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or a generic agent prompt. Use `hk agent hooks` for an optional Codex or Claude Code stop hook, or a VS Code task. Hook output is deliberately a snippet rather than an automatic installation: inspect its effect on your workflow before enabling it.

content.thinking:
Examining the design goals of the 'agent' feature reveals a focus on enhancing AI coding agents, particularly by improving how they interact with traditional code analysis tools. The aim is to mitigate potential issues like misinterpretations and unintended command execution that arise from chaotic terminal outputs. The goal also involves addressing the challenge of keeping the agent informed about the project's structure.


This agent feature leverages structured interfaces and safe sandboxing for AI code agents, focusing on code checking and automated fixing. It offers a structured tool interface via a built-in server, providing structured diagnostic information, diffs, and execution status. The feature also automatically generates agent instructions and hooks to ensure the agents adhere to defined guidelines and incorporate automated checks.

content.text:
**`hk` 的 Agent 功能**是专门为 **AI Coding Agent**（如 Pi、Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、VS Code 等）设计的**代码质量保障与交互接口**。

它解决的核心痛点是：传统 linter 输出多为终端非结构化文本，AI Agent 容易解析错误、难以精准定位问题，甚至可能误执行具有破坏性的修复命令。`hk` 为 Agent 提供了一套**结构化、安全受限、可交互**的检查与修复机制。

---

### 一、核心功能模块

#### 1. 内置 MCP 服务器 (`hk mcp`)
`hk` 内置了遵循 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 的标准 STDIO 服务器：
- **结构化工具调用**：Agent 不需要去猜终端命令，直接通过 MCP Tools 触发 `check` / `fix`、获取步骤耗时、分页日志和结构化诊断信息。
- **安全沙箱限制**：MCP 服务器严格锁定在当前项目根目录，Agent 无法通过它注入任意未授权的系统路径或危险 Shell 命令。
- **富交互 Dashboard（MCP App）**：在支持 MCP App 的客户端中，可以直接在 UI 中渲染可视化的检查面板（查看每个 Step 耗时、按文件分组的报错、代码 diff 视图）。
- **一键生成 MCP 配置**：
  ```bash
  hk agent mcp --target vscode
  hk agent mcp --target claude-code
  hk agent mcp --target claude-desktop
  hk agent mcp --target codex
  ```

---

#### 2. Agent 规范指令生成器 (`hk agent instructions`)
为各种 Agent 自动生成适合写入 `AGENTS.md`、`CLAUDE.md` 或 System Prompt 的上下文规范说明：
```bash
hk agent instructions --target claude-code
hk agent instructions --target codex
hk agent instructions --target generic
```
执行后会输出一段专为该 Agent 定制的指令，告诉 Agent：
- 项目中定义了哪些 lint / format 步骤。
- 编辑完代码后应该如何调用 `hk` 进行自检。
- 如何在交付代码前通过 `hk` 验证修改。

---

#### 3. Agent 自动化钩子生成 (`hk agent hooks`)
```bash
hk agent hooks --target claude-code
hk agent hooks --target codex
hk agent hooks --target vscode
```
生成 Agent 专用的 Stop Hook 或 VS Code Task。例如配置在 Agent 即将完成回复/提交前，自动触发一次 `hk` 检查，未通过则阻止提交并要求 Agent 自行修复。

---

### 二、AI Agent 推荐的安全工作流 (Safe Agent Workflow)

`hk` 针对 Agent 交互做了专门的命令行优化：

1. **`--safe` 安全防护**：
   ```bash
   hk run check --safe
   ```
   在任何 Step 开始前进行静态预检，如果包含未知的破坏性命令则直接拒绝执行，防止 Agent 造成代码意外损毁。

2. **精确定位修改文件（Null-delimited 文件流）**：
   Agent 可以仅检查本次改动的文件，避免全量扫描浪费 token 和时间：
   ```bash
   {
     git diff --name-only -z
     git diff --cached --name-only -z
     git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z
   } | hk run check --files0-from - --safe --format jsonl
   ```

3. **原生机器可读格式 (`--format json` / `jsonl`)**：
   输出标准的 JSON / JSONL 诊断信息（包含文件名、行号、列号、规则名、严重级别），方便 Agent 精确读取报错并直接定位修改代码。

---

### 三、总结

| 能力维度 | 传统工具 / pre-commit | hk Agent 功能 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **与 Agent 协议对接** | 只能靠 bash 执行命令 | 原生内置 **MCP Server** 与 MCP App Dashboard |
| **输出格式** | 终端彩色字符串（需正则解析） | 原生 **JSON / JSONL 结构化诊断** |
| **安全性控制** | 无限制执行 | **`--safe`** 预检拦截破坏性操作，根目录严格限定 |
| **Agent Prompt 集成** | 手写 prompt 告诉 agent 规范 | **`hk agent instructions`** 一键生成标准 prompt |

content.text:
=== generic ===
## Using hk from a coding agent

Inspect and plan before running. Scope checks to changed files with `--files0-from` and use `--cd` to select the project root. Prefer `--safe`, inspect command effects, and require approval for unknown or destructive commands. Consume JSON or JSONL diagnostics while retaining raw output, and always review the diff produced by a fix. MCP clients should use `inspect_project`, `plan`, safe run tools, paged output, and `get_diff` rather than invoking arbitrary shell commands.
=== claude-code ===
## hk

- Ask the hk MCP server to inspect the project and plan checks before execution.
- Scope work to changed files (`--files0-from` accepts exact NUL-delimited paths) and use `--cd` for another project root.
- Prefer safe checks and safe fixes. Inspect command effects and ask before any unknown or destructive command.
- Read normalized diagnostics from structured results, then inspect the patch before reporting or committing a fix.
- If MCP is unavailable, run `hk run check --format jsonl --safe`; the final event is the authoritative summary.
=== codex ===
## hk

- Before changing files, inspect the project with `hk mcp` or `hk run check --safe --format json`.
- Scope checks to the files you changed. For exact filenames, write a NUL-delimited list and use `--files0-from`; use `--cd` instead of changing hk's process-wide directory.
- Inspect each planned command's effect. Prefer `--safe`; never run an unknown or destructive command without explicit user approval.
- Consume normalized diagnostics from JSON/JSONL, preserve raw tool output for debugging, and review the resulting diff after fixes.
- Use `hk run check --safe --format jsonl` for streaming lifecycle events. A final summary is emitted even when a step fails.

Considering the simplicity of the current system, the dual management approach (skill + agent) introduces overhead if the agent's functionality is directly tied to a small set of skills. A single file might be sufficient for a straightforward agent, streamlining access and reducing complexity.

However, recognizing potential future expansion and modularity, the dual approach provides a clearer structure. Evaluate the likelihood of the agent's complexity growing and the benefits of easier skill reuse.


AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md serve as persistent, background context, ideal for project-wide rules and quick references. This approach faces limitations concerning token usage and the inability to provide detailed operational expertise on demand. Skills, on the other hand, provide in-depth, on-demand operational knowledge, standardized playbooks, and progressive execution, although they introduce added complexity if a task can be handled by the agent directly.


The optimal approach appears to be a dual-layer structure comprising both a lightweight configuration file and a dedicated skill repository. This design balances simplicity for routine tasks with the need for detailed operational guidance in specialized scenarios.

The lightweight file acts as a baseline requirement, ensuring that agents are aware of essential project-level checks.  The dedicated skill repository provides in-depth operational knowledge when addressing complex tasks requiring specialized expertise.

content.text:
推荐采用 **「Skill + AGENTS.md 双层管理」** 模式。

在实际工程和 Agent 交互中，这两种方式的定位是完全互补的——类似于 **“日常守门员”** 和 **“专家特种兵”** 的分工。

---

### 一、为什么“单文件”会有痛点？

* **单写在 `AGENTS.md` 太长**：如果把 Pkl 语法、如何写自定义 Step、CI 集成、Stash 冲突排查、150+ 内置 linter 映射等详细 SOP 都塞进 `AGENTS.md`，每个日常会话（哪怕只是改个变量名）都会被迫吃掉大量 Token 且容易稀释注意力。
* **单写在 `AGENTS.md` 太短**：如果只写三五行命令，Agent 在日常修改代码时只知道跑 `hk check`，但一旦遇到**“要新增一个 linter”、“hk 报语法错误”、“要排查 hook 为什么没触发”**等复杂任务时，Agent 就抓瞎了。
* **只写 Skill 不写 `AGENTS.md`**：如果只有 Skill，Agent 在处理普通的业务需求（比如修复一个 C++ 语音录制 bug）时可能根本不会触发该 Skill，导致 Agent 在任务结束时直接忽略代码校验和格式化。

---

### 二、双层管理的职责分工

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  AGENTS.md (日常轻量契约 / 始终载入)                           │
│  • 职责：底线规范与快速指令                                  │
│  • 场景：任何代码变更结束前的快速自检与格式修复              │
│  • Token 消耗：极低 (30~50 行)                               │
└──────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                               │
            遇到复杂 Hook 配置/排错/扩展需求时按需唤醒
                               │
                               ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Skill: hk-workflow (按需唤醒 / 专家知识库)                  │
│  • 职责：深度运维 SOP、Pkl 语法指南、自定义 Step 模板、排错指南│
│  • 场景：配置新 hook、写测试、排查 stash/lock 异常、对接 CI  │
│  • Token 消耗：按需加载，不污染日常对话                      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 三、具体实现设计

#### 1. `AGENTS.md`：轻量日常契约（作为守门规则）
只保留核心行为约束与常用速查指令：
- 本项目使用 `hk` 进行代码格式与质量管控。
- 任务完成前必须执行 `hk run check --safe` 或 `hk check`。
- 格式问题优先使用 `hk fix` 修复并核对 `git diff`。
- 如果需要扩展或修改 Hook 配置，调用 `hk-workflow` Skill。

#### 2. `Skill`（如 `hk-workflow`）：专项操作手册
放置在 `.pi/skills/hk-workflow/SKILL.md`（或全局/项目 Skill 目录），包含：
- **Pkl 配置语法范式**：`amends`, `Builtins`, `Step` 结构定义。
- **项目专项 Step 模板**：
  - C++ `clang-format` / `clang-tidy` 适配模板
  - Python / Shell / JSON 检查适配
  - i18n 脚本与 CMake 语法检查
- **常见问题与故障排查（Troubleshooting）**：
  - Stash 恢复与锁定冲突处理（`patch-file` vs `git`）
  - `--files0-from` 的安全批处理
  - CI 与本地行为不一致排查

---

### 四、建议

如果赞同这种架构，我们可以：
1. **精简并固化 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`** 作为日常常驻约束；
2. **创建一套 `hk-workflow` Skill**，将 `hk` 的深度配置能力、Pkl 模板与排错 SOP 沉淀为标准技能；
3. **完成本项目的 `hk.pkl` 与 `mise.toml` 配置**并进行实测验证。

---

### 一、单文件 vs 双管理（`AGENTS.md` + `Skill`）的对比

在以“**本项目开发与贡献**”为主体的视角下，两者的差异如下：

#### 方案 A：单文件（仅 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`）
* **做法**：将项目架构、CMake/mise 构建命令、C++20 代码规范、`hk` 代码检查、模块职责、测试与提交要求全部写在一个 `AGENTS.md` 里。
* **优点**：结构最简单直接，单文件即项目全貌，任何 Agent 进仓库第一时间就能读懂。
* **局限**：当项目扩展到包含复杂的专项业务（例如：编写新的 ASR 厂商适配器规范、多发行版打包与发版流程、PipeWire 音频流调试流程等）时，单文件会变得非常臃肿，且每次简单对话都会全量注入这些深度专项目录。

#### 方案 B：双管理（`AGENTS.md` 作为总览契约 + `Skill` 作为专项扩展 SOP）—— **更推荐**
* **`AGENTS.md`（项目通用全景与日常开发契约 —— 常驻上下文）**：
  面向任何进仓库写代码的 Agent，提供通用的核心指引：
  1. **项目定位与核心架构**（`src/addon` 插件、`src/daemon` 录音与推理服务、`src/cli`、`src/common`）。
  2. **日常构建与调试指令**（`mise run build`、`mise run dev`、CMake 预设）。
  3. **代码规范与质量门禁**（C++20 规范、`hk check` / `hk fix`、i18n 校验）。
  4. **提交与贡献规范**。
* **`Skill`（特定高阶任务的专家操作手册 —— 按需唤醒）**：
  当 Agent 接到特定复杂业务任务时，按需加载深度的 SOP：
  - **Skill 1：`vinput-provider-extension`**（如何新增/调试 ASR 厂商脚本或 LLM 场景适配器、数据契约、i18n 配置）。
  - **Skill 2：`vinput-packaging-release`**（如何进行多发行版打包：Debian Docker、Flatpak、AUR PKGBUILD、Nix 与发版流程）。

---

### 二、针对 `fcitx5-vinput` 的推荐落地结构

如果我们采用 **双管理** 模式，具体设计如下：

#### 1. `AGENTS.md`（项目开发全局契约）
```markdown
# fcitx5-vinput Agent Guide

## 1. Project Overview & Architecture
- `src/addon/`: Fcitx5 input method addon (UI, DBus client, key triggers)
- `src/daemon/`: ASR daemon (PipeWire audio capture, sherpa-onnx, cloud ASR, LLM scenes)
- `src/cli/`: `vinput` command-line utility
- `src/common/`: Shared models, DBus interfaces, configuration definitions

## 2. Toolchain & Build System
- Managed by `mise` and CMake Presets:
  - Configure Debug: `mise run dev`
  - Build: `mise run build` or `mise run build-debug`
  - Install: `sudo mise run install`

## 3. Code Quality & Formatting (hk)
- Tool: `hk` with pre-configured `clang-format`, `mise`, `check-i18n`, `json-validate`.
- **Pre-commit verification**: Always run `hk run check --safe` before completing code tasks.
- **Auto-formatting**: Run `hk fix` to format C++ code and configuration files.

## 4. Coding Conventions
- C++20 standard, strict compiler warnings.
- Keep user-visible strings wrapped in `_()` / gettext for i18n.
```

#### 2. 项目专属 `Skill`（按需沉淀高阶 SOP）
例如在 `.pi/skills/vinput-dev/SKILL.md` 中沉淀更深度的业务知识：
- 如何为 daemon 添加新的 D-Bus 接口或事件。
- 如何在 `src/daemon/audio/` 中调试 PipeWire 录音缓冲区与冷启动。
- 如何编写和测试 `scripts/check-i18n.py` 关联的多语言 `.po` 资源。
- `hk.pkl` 的自定义步骤维护。

---

--skill <path>                 Load a skill file or directory (can be used multiple times)
  --no-skills, -ns               Disable skills discovery and loading

> pi can create skills. Ask it to build one for your use case.

# Skills

Skills are self-contained capability packages that the agent loads on-demand. A skill provides specialized workflows, setup instructions, helper scripts, and reference documentation for specific tasks.

Pi implements the [Agent Skills standard](https://agentskills.io/specification), warning about most violations but remaining lenient. Pi allows skill names to differ from their parent directory even though the standard disallows it; that rule is suboptimal for shared skill directories used across multiple agent harnesses.

## Table of Contents

- [Locations](#locations)
- [How Skills Work](#how-skills-work)
- [Skill Commands](#skill-commands)
- [Skill Structure](#skill-structure)
- [Frontmatter](#frontmatter)
- [Validation](#validation)
- [Example](#example)
- [Skill Repositories](#skill-repositories)

## Locations

> **Security:** Skills can instruct the model to perform any action and may include executable code the model invokes. Review skill content before use.

Pi loads skills from:

- Global:
  - `~/.pi/agent/skills/`
  - `~/.agents/skills/`
- Project (only after the project is trusted):
  - `.pi/skills/`
  - `.agents/skills/` in `cwd` and ancestor directories (up to git repo root, or filesystem root when not in a repo)
- Packages: `skills/` directories or `pi.skills` entries in `package.json`
- Settings: `skills` array with files or directories
- CLI: `--skill <path>` (repeatable, additive even with `--no-skills`)

Discovery rules:
- In `~/.pi/agent/skills/` and `.pi/skills/`, direct root `.md` files are discovered as individual skills when they have valid skill frontmatter with a non-empty `description`
- In all skill locations, directories containing `SKILL.md` are discovered recursively
- In `~/.agents/skills/` and project `.agents/skills/`, root `.md` files are ignored, but nested `.md` files in grouping folders are discovered when they declare skill frontmatter
- Root Markdown files other than `SKILL.md` that do not look like skills are ignored silently

Disable discovery with `--no-skills` (explicit `--skill` paths still load).

### Using Skills from Other Harnesses

To use skills from Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, add their directories to settings:

```json
{
  "skills": [
    "~/.claude/skills",
    "~/.codex/skills"
  ]
}
```

For project-level Claude Code skills, add to `.pi/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "skills": ["../.claude/skills"]
}
```

## How Skills Work

1. At startup, pi scans skill locations and extracts names and descriptions
2. The system prompt includes available skills in XML format per the [specification](https://agentskills.io/integrate-skills)
3. When a task matches, the agent uses `read` to load the full SKILL.md (models don't always do this; use prompting or `/skill:name` to force it)
4. The agent follows the instructions, using relative paths to reference scripts and assets

This is progressive disclosure: only descriptions are always in context, full instructions load on-demand.

## Skill Commands

Skills register as `/skill:name` commands:

```bash
/skill:brave-search           # Load and execute the skill
/skill:pdf-tools extract      # Load skill with arguments
```

Arguments after the command are appended to the skill content as `User: <args>`.

Toggle skill commands via `/settings` in interactive mode or in `settings.json`:

```json
{
  "enableSkillCommands": true
}
```

## Skill Structure

A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md` file. Everything else is freeform.

```
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md              # Required: frontmatter + instructions
├── scripts/              # Helper scripts

为了保证**最大通用性与跨 Agent 兼容性**，推荐使用 **`.agents/skills/`**（注意是复数 `agents`）。

---

### 一、为什么选 `.agents/skills/`？

1. **符合行业开放标准（[Agent Skills Specification](https://agentskills.io/)）**：
   - `.agents/skills/` 是开源 Agent 生态（包括 `skills` CLI、OpenCLI 等）制定的通用开放规范。
   - 它是中立命名的目录，不绑定任何特定 AI 框架。

2. **跨 Harness 兼容性更好**：
   - **Pi**：原生扫描并完全支持 `.agents/skills/` 和 `~/.agents/skills/`。
   - **Claude Code / Codex / Cursor 等**：识别中立的 `.agents/` 目录结构，其他开发者克隆你的开源项目时，无论用什么 Agent 都可以无缝识别，而不会被特异性的 `.pi/` 目录限制。
   - **`.pi/skills/`**：是 Pi 的专有项目目录，其他 Agent 默认不会主动扫描它。

---

### 二、推荐的最终通用项目结构

```
fcitx5-vinput/
├── AGENTS.md                   # [通用入口契约] 所有 Agent 进入项目的第一站
├── CLAUDE.md                   # [符号链接或兼容文件 -> AGENTS.md]
├── hk.pkl                      # [代码门禁与质量管理] hk 配置文件
├── mise.toml                   # [环境与任务管理] mise 配置文件
│
└── .agents/
    └── skills/
        └── vinput-dev/
            ├── SKILL.md        # [专项操作手册] 深度开发、构建、排错 SOP
            └── scripts/        # (可选) 辅助自动化脚本
```

---

### 三、两者的标准写法

#### 1. 根目录 `AGENTS.md`（轻量通用契约，30~50行）
作为所有 Agent 的全局护栏，简洁地声明：
- 项目核心架构（Addon / Daemon / CLI / Common）。
- 构建/测试命令（`mise run build`、`mise run dev`）。
- 代码校验底线（`hk check` / `hk fix`）。
- 提示 Agent：“在处理复杂扩展（如新增 ASR Provider/打包/D-Bus 调试）时，请使用 `.agents/skills/vinput-dev/SKILL.md`”。

#### 2. `.agents/skills/vinput-dev/SKILL.md`（标准 Skill 格式）
```markdown
---
name: vinput-dev
description: Development, architecture, debugging, extension, and packaging workflows for fcitx5-vinput. Use when modifying daemon/addon code, adding ASR providers/LLM scenes, debugging audio, running CMake builds, or managing multi-distro packaging.
---

# fcitx5-vinput Development Skill

## Architecture & Data Flow
...

## Build & Debugging SOP
...

## Adding New Cloud ASR / LLM Adapters
...

## Multi-distro Packaging
...
```

---

这样设计既保证了任何 Agent 都能在第一时间读到轻量的 `AGENTS.md` 遵守代码底线，又能在需要深度开发时按标准加载 `.agents/skills/` 中的专项手册。

# fcitx5-vinput Agent Guide

Guidelines and baseline rules for AI coding agents working on `fcitx5-vinput`.

---

## 1. Project Overview & Architecture

`fcitx5-vinput` is a voice input system for Fcitx5 providing local (sherpa-onnx) and cloud ASR, LLM post-processing, and cross-distro packaging.

- **`src/addon/`**: Fcitx5 input method addon (Qt/C++, hotkey triggers like `F8`, push-to-talk, D-Bus client).
- **`src/daemon/`**: Core daemon (`vinput-daemon`), handles PipeWire audio recording, sherpa-onnx inference, cloud ASR engines, LLM scene transformations, D-Bus service (`org.fcitx.Vinput`).
- **`src/cli/`**: `vinput` CLI tool for status, config management, and manual triggering.
- **`src/common/`**: Shared types, configuration structs (`nlohmann-json`), D-Bus XML interfaces.
- **`po/` & `i18n/`**: Translations (Gettext and Qt `.ts` / `.qm`).

For detailed architectural flow, audio debugging, and extension SOPs, refer to the skill at `.agents/skills/vinput-dev/SKILL.md`.

---

## 2. Toolchain & Build System

The project uses `mise` for environment and task orchestration, with CMake presets:

- **Configure Debug Build**: `mise run dev`
- **Configure Release Build**: `mise run configure-release`
- **Build**: `mise run build` (Release) or `mise run build-debug` (Debug)
- **Install locally**: `sudo mise run install`
- **Diagnostic Check**: `mise run doctor`

---

## 3. Code Quality & Verification (hk CLI)

This repository uses **`hk`** (Git Hook Manager) with `mise` to enforce formatting and validation:

- **Run checks on changed files (Recommended before completing tasks)**:
  ```bash
  {
    git diff --name-only -z
    git diff --cached --name-only -z
    git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z
  } | hk run check --files0-from - --safe
  ```
- **Auto-fix formatting violations** (formats C++ with `.clang-format`, configs, etc.):
  ```bash
  hk fix
  ```
- **Full repository check**:
  ```bash
  hk check
  ```
- **Static analysis**:
  ```bash
  mise run tidy
  ```

---

## 4. Coding & Contribution Rules

description: Deep development, debugging, extension, and packaging workflows for fcitx5-vinput. Use when modifying daemon/addon C++20 code, debugging PipeWire audio capture or D-Bus events, adding cloud ASR providers or LLM scene adapters, updating i18n translations, or building multi-distro packages (Debian, Flatpak, Arch, Nix).
---

# fcitx5-vinput Developer Manual

This skill provides specialized instructions, architectural references, debugging SOPs, and packaging guides for developing and contributing to `fcitx5-vinput`.

---

## 1. System Architecture & Component Boundaries

```
[ User Hotkey (F8 / PTT) ]
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  src/addon/ (Fcitx5 Addon, C++/Qt)     │
│  - Catches key events & triggers       │
│  - Displays floating UI indicator      │
│  - Commits recognized text to input    │
└───────────────────┬────────────────────┘
                    │ D-Bus (org.fcitx.Vinput)
                    ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  src/daemon/ (vinput-daemon)           │
│  ├─ audio/   : PipeWire Stream Capture │
│  ├─ asr/     : Local (sherpa-onnx) &   │
│  │             Cloud ASR Providers     │
│  ├─ llm/     : Scene Post-processing   │
│  └─ dbus/    : Service Dispatcher      │
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Key Subdirectories
- **`src/addon/`**: Fcitx5 addon implementation. Interacts with Fcitx5 input contexts and windowing system.
- **`src/daemon/`**: Background daemon. Runs as a systemd user service (`vinput-daemon.service`).
- **`src/cli/`**: Standalone `vinput` CLI for manual recording, profile switching, and status inspection.
- **`src/common/`**: Shared structs, configuration loading (`nlohmann::json`), and D-Bus interface definitions.
- **`data/`**: Default configurations and icon resources.
- **`po/` & `i18n/`**: Localization catalogs (`fcitx5-vinput.pot`, `zh_CN.po`, etc.).

---

## 2. Build & Development SOP

### Prerequisites
- CMake 3.20+, Ninja/Mold (optional but recommended), Clang/GCC supporting C++20.
- Dependencies: `fcitx5`, `pipewire`, `libcurl`, `nlohmann-json`, `CLI11`, `Qt6`.

### Common Tasks via `mise`
```bash
# Configure debug preset (with address sanitizers / debug symbols)
mise run dev

# Build Debug / Release
mise run build-debug
mise run build

# Install locally to /usr (or custom prefix)
sudo mise run install

# Diagnostic health check (verifies service, binary paths, CMake cache)
mise run doctor

# Run clang-tidy static analysis
mise run tidy
```

---

## 3. Code Quality & Verification (`hk`)

The repository uses `hk` to enforce code standards with zero-latency parallel checks.

### Pre-commit Verification Workflow
Always run checks before finishing code edits:

```bash
# 1. Check changed files safely
{
  git diff --name-only -z
  git diff --cached --name-only -z
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z
} | hk run check --files0-from - --safe

# 2. Automatically fix formatting issues (clang-format, mise, whitespace)
hk fix

# 3. Verify all checks pass
hk check
```

### Modifying Hook Rules (`hk.pkl`)
- `hk.pkl` defines the linters via Apple Pkl.
- Builtin formatters include: `Builtins.clang_format`, `Builtins.mise`, `Builtins.trailing_whitespace`, `Builtins.newlines`.
- Custom steps (e.g. `check-i18n`, `json-validate`) execute via shell commands.
- Validate configuration changes with `hk validate`.

---

## 4. Audio & PipeWire Subsystem Debugging

### Inspecting Daemon Logs
```bash
# Follow live daemon logs
journalctl --user -u vinput-daemon.service -f -n 100

# Run daemon directly in foreground for debugging
vinput-daemon --debug
```

### Benchmarking Audio Capture Cold-Start
```bash
bash scripts/bench-capture-cold-start.sh
```

---

## 5. Adding Cloud ASR Providers & LLM Adapters

All cloud provider scripts and LLM post-processing scene adapters follow the [vinput-registry](https://github.com/xifan2333/vinput-registry) specification:

### Script Rules
1. **Self-contained**: Must use Python 3 standard library only (`urllib.request`, `json`, `hashlib`, etc.) — zero pip dependencies.
2. **Entry point**: Standard `entry.py` receiving arguments via CLI/JSON stdin and outputting structured JSON to stdout.
3. **i18n**: Provide localization entries in `en_US.json` and `zh_CN.json`.
4. **Documentation**: Include a concise `README.md` explaining API keys and endpoints.

---

## 6. Multi-Distro Packaging SOP

```bash
# Debian / Ubuntu package build via Docker
mise run deb

# Flatpak build & bundle
mise run flatpak-build
mise run flatpak-bundle

# Generate updated Arch Linux PKGBUILD
bash scripts/render-arch-pkgbuild.sh

# Cut a new release tag
mise run release <version_number>
```

# vinput-registry

Registry repository for vinput resources.

## Layout

- `registry/`: top-level resource indexes
- `i18n/`: resource display text, one file per language
- `resources/providers/<folder>/<name>/`: cloud ASR provider scripts
- `resources/adapters/<folder>/<name>/`: managed local adaptor scripts

## Resource Rules

- Resource ids are stable machine identifiers.
- Resource ids should follow `<kinds>.<folder>.<name>`.
- `short_id` is required for every resource item.
- `short_id` is only for human interaction in CLI/GUI/logs.
- `short_id` must not be used for storage paths, download paths, or internal
  resource resolution.
- Download-related URLs use array form for fallback
- Resource display text is stored in i18n files as:
  - `<id>.title`
  - `<id>.description`
- Script resources should keep:
  - `entry.py`
  - `README.md`

## Resource Fields

All resource items should contain:

- `id`: stable machine identifier
- `short_id`: short human-facing identifier

Provider items additionally contain:

- `stream`: `true` for streaming scripts, `false` for one-shot scripts
- `envs`: runtime environment variable declarations for local execution

## Provider Env Rules

Provider env names should use the `VINPUT_ASR_*` namespace.

Shared provider envs should keep stable names and meanings:

- `VINPUT_ASR_API_KEY`: bearer-style API credential
- `VINPUT_ASR_APP_ID`: app identifier for providers that require it separately
- `VINPUT_ASR_ACCESS_TOKEN`: token credential for providers that do not use API keys
- `VINPUT_ASR_URL`: full request or websocket endpoint override
- `VINPUT_ASR_BASE_URL`: base endpoint override when the script constructs the final path
- `VINPUT_ASR_MODEL`: remote model identifier
- `VINPUT_ASR_LANGUAGE`: explicit transcription language hint
- `VINPUT_ASR_PROMPT`: optional recognition prompt or bias text
- `VINPUT_ASR_TIMEOUT`: end-to-end network timeout in seconds
- `VINPUT_ASR_FINISH_GRACE_SECS`: extra wait time after local `finish` before closing
- `VINPUT_ASR_ENABLE_VAD`: enable server-side VAD when the provider supports it
- `VINPUT_ASR_VAD_THRESHOLD`: provider VAD sensitivity threshold
- `VINPUT_ASR_VAD_PREFIX_PADDING_MS`: audio padding kept before detected speech
- `VINPUT_ASR_VAD_SILENCE_DURATION_MS`: silence duration used to close a speech turn

Provider-specific envs are allowed when the upstream API exposes features that do
not map cleanly to the shared set. These should still use the `VINPUT_ASR_*`
prefix and should be listed after the shared envs in `registry/providers.json`.

## Current Scope

- `models.json`: local ASR models
- `providers.json`: cloud ASR provider scripts
- `adapters.json`: managed local LLM adapter scripts

## `vinput_model` Rules

For local ASR models, `vinput_model` is runtime-facing metadata and should use
the following top-level shape:

- `backend`: local backend selector such as `sherpa-offline` or
  `sherpa-streaming`
- `runtime`: `online` or `offline`
- `family`: `sherpa-onnx` C API family name
- `recognizer`: recognizer config fields
- `model`: model config fields

Field naming should stay as close as possible to `sherpa-onnx` C API naming.

## Terminology

- `models`: local ASR model assets
- `providers`: cloud ASR service scripts
- `adapters`: managed local LLM adaptor scripts
- `backend`: local ASR engine/backend selector for model runtime metadata

---
name: vinput-dev
description: Deep development, debugging, extension, cross-repo ecosystem integration, and packaging workflows for fcitx5-vinput. Use when modifying daemon/addon C++20 code, working with related repositories (vinput-registry, aur-auto), debugging PipeWire audio capture or D-Bus events, adding cloud ASR providers or LLM scene adapters, updating i18n translations, or building multi-distro packages (Debian, Flatpak, Arch, Nix).
---

# fcitx5-vinput Developer Manual & Ecosystem Guide

This skill provides specialized instructions, architectural references, debugging SOPs, cross-repo workflows, and packaging guides for developing and contributing to `fcitx5-vinput` and its related ecosystem repositories.

---

## 1. Ecosystem Overview & Repository Boundaries

The `fcitx5-vinput` voice input system consists of three GitHub repositories:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput (Core Engine)                                  │
│  Path: . (or ~/Code/fcitx5-vinput)                                     │
│  • C++20 Fcitx5 addon, UI, PipeWire capture, daemon & CLI              │
│  • Local sherpa-onnx inference runtime & D-Bus service                 │
│  • Manages releases, Debian / Flatpak / Nix packages                   │
└───────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
         ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                     ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  xifan2333/vinput-registry           │  │  xifan2333/aur-auto                  │
│  Path: ~/Code/vinput-registry        │  │  Path: ~/Code/aur-auto               │
│  • Index for local models & providers│  │  • Arch Linux AUR package automation │
│  • Cloud ASR provider scripts        │  │  • pkgs/fcitx5-vinput-bin/ tracking  │
│  • LLM scene adapter scripts         │  │  • Clean chroot builds & AUR publish │
│  • Multi-language resource text      │  │                                      │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘  └──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Core Architecture & Component Boundaries (`fcitx5-vinput`)

```
[ User Hotkey (F8 / PTT) ]
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  src/addon/ (Fcitx5 Addon, C++/Qt)     │
│  - Catches key events & triggers       │
│  - Displays floating UI indicator      │
│  - Commits recognized text to input    │
└───────────────────┬────────────────────┘
                    │ D-Bus (org.fcitx.Vinput)
                    ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  src/daemon/ (vinput-daemon)           │
│  ├─ audio/   : PipeWire Stream Capture │
│  ├─ asr/     : Local (sherpa-onnx) &   │
│  │             Cloud ASR Providers     │
│  ├─ llm/     : Scene Post-processing   │
│  └─ dbus/    : Service Dispatcher      │
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Key Subdirectories in Core Repo
- **`src/addon/`**: Fcitx5 addon implementation. Interacts with Fcitx5 input contexts and windowing system.
- **`src/daemon/`**: Background daemon. Runs as a systemd user service (`vinput-daemon.service`).
- **`src/cli/`**: Standalone `vinput` CLI for manual recording, profile switching, and status inspection.
- **`src/common/`**: Shared structs, configuration loading (`nlohmann::json`), and D-Bus interface definitions.
- **`data/`**: Default configurations and icon resources.
- **`po/` & `i18n/`**: Localization catalogs (`fcitx5-vinput.pot`, `zh_CN.po`, etc.).

---

## 3. Build & Development SOP (Core Repo)

### Common Tasks via `mise`
```bash
# Configure debug preset (with address sanitizers / debug symbols)
mise run dev

# Build Debug / Release
mise run build-debug
mise run build

# Install locally to /usr (or custom prefix)
sudo mise run install

# Diagnostic health check (verifies service, binary paths, CMake cache)
mise run doctor

# Run clang-tidy static analysis
mise run tidy
```

---

## 4. Code Quality & Verification (`hk`)

The repository uses `hk` to enforce code standards with zero-latency parallel checks.

### Pre-commit Verification Workflow
Always run checks before finishing code edits:

```bash
# 1. Check changed files safely
{
  git diff --name-only -z
  git diff --cached --name-only -z
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z
} | hk run check --files0-from - --safe

# 2. Automatically fix formatting issues (clang-format, mise, whitespace)
hk fix

# 3. Verify all checks pass
hk check
```

### Modifying Hook Rules (`hk.pkl`)
- `hk.pkl` defines the linters via Apple Pkl.
- Builtin formatters include: `Builtins.clang_format`, `Builtins.mise`, `Builtins.trailing_whitespace`, `Builtins.newlines`.
- Custom steps (e.g. `check-i18n`, `json-validate`) execute via shell commands.
- Validate configuration changes with `hk validate`.

---

## 5. Working with `vinput-registry` (`~/Code/vinput-registry`)

When adding or updating ASR providers, LLM scenes, or local model catalogs, work in `~/Code/vinput-registry`.

### Repository Layout
- `registry/`: Index metadata files (`models.json`, `providers.json`, `adapters.json`).
- `resources/providers/<folder>/<name>/`: Cloud ASR provider scripts (`entry.py` + `README.md`).
- `resources/adapters/<folder>/<name>/`: LLM scene adapter scripts (`entry.py` + `README.md`).
- `i18n/`: Multilingual display text (`en_US.json`, `zh_CN.json`).

### Rules for Scripts & Adapters
1. **Self-contained**: Must use Python 3 standard library only (`urllib.request`, `json`, `hashlib`, etc.) — zero pip dependencies.
2. **Resource IDs**: Stable machine identifiers following `<kinds>.<folder>.<name>` (e.g., `providers.doubao.asr-stream`).
3. **Short ID**: Human-readable identifier for CLI/GUI display (e.g., `doubao-stream`).
4. **Environment Variables**: Use standard `VINPUT_ASR_*` namespaces:
   - `VINPUT_ASR_API_KEY`: API credential / Bearer token
   - `VINPUT_ASR_APP_ID`: App ID (if required)
   - `VINPUT_ASR_URL` / `VINPUT_ASR_BASE_URL`: Endpoint overrides
   - `VINPUT_ASR_MODEL`: Remote model name
   - `VINPUT_ASR_LANGUAGE`: Language hint
   - `VINPUT_ASR_PROMPT`: Context / prompt bias
5. **i18n Keys**: Add `<id>.title` and `<id>.description` into both `i18n/en_US.json` and `i18n/zh_CN.json`.

---

## 6. Working with `aur-auto` (`~/Code/aur-auto`)

Arch Linux binary package (`fcitx5-vinput-bin`) publication is automated in `~/Code/aur-auto`.

### Package Structure (`pkgs/fcitx5-vinput-bin/`)
- `upstream.sh`: Fetches the latest release version and asset download URLs from `xifan2333/fcitx5-vinput` on GitHub.
- `PKGBUILD`: Template for extracting pre-built binaries, installing systemd user units, icons, desktop files, and licenses.
- `fcitx5-vinput-bin.install`: Post-install hooks (reminding users to reload systemd user daemon).

### Release Flow to AUR
1. A new GitHub release tag is pushed in `fcitx5-vinput` (`mise run release <version>`).
2. GitHub Actions in `aur-auto` triggers `build-and-publish.yml`.
3. `aur-auto` runs `upstream.sh` to fetch release assets, generates updated `PKGBUILD`, builds the package in a clean chroot container, and pushes the commit directly to the AUR Git repo.

---

## 7. Audio & PipeWire Subsystem Debugging

### Inspecting Daemon Logs
```bash
# Follow live daemon logs
journalctl --user -u vinput-daemon.service -f -n 100

# Run daemon directly in foreground for debugging
vinput-daemon --debug
```

### Benchmarking Audio Capture Cold-Start
```bash
bash scripts/bench-capture-cold-start.sh
```

---

## 8. Multi-Distro Packaging SOP

```bash
# Debian / Ubuntu package build via Docker
mise run deb

# Flatpak build & bundle
mise run flatpak-build
mise run flatpak-bundle

# Generate updated Arch Linux PKGBUILD locally
bash scripts/render-arch-pkgbuild.sh

# Cut a new release tag
mise run release <version_number>
```

`fcitx5-vinput`'s build process leverages GitHub Actions through several workflows. The core CI workflow covers standard builds and tests. Distribution-specific packages are managed by a separate workflow that supports multiple channels. Release builds are triggered either by version tags or manual dispatch, and there is a workflow dedicated to channel installation verification.


GitHub Actions is preferred for builds due to its access to consistent, clean, and isolated environments that include full dependency caching and cross-compilation toolchains. Local compilation is less reliable due to potential missing dependencies and environment inconsistencies. To manage builds, the recommendation is to trigger and monitor remote workflows whenever possible, reserving local builds for rapid, incremental development.

## 3. Build & CI Workflows (Prioritize GitHub Actions)

### Core Principle: Prefer Remote GitHub Actions over Local Heavy Builds
To keep local machines clean, avoid toolchain drift, and leverage cloud caching (Cachix, ccache, multi-distro Docker runners), **always prioritize running compilation and package builds via GitHub Actions** rather than building heavy artifacts locally.

### GitHub Actions Workflows Reference

| Workflow | File | Trigger Command | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CI Build & Test** | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `gh workflow run ci.yml` | Standard build and test verification on Ubuntu runners. |
| **Packaging Channels** | `.github/workflows/channels.yml` | `mise run channels` or `gh workflow run channels.yml` | Builds across all distribution channels (PPA, COPR, Flatpak, Debian). |
| **Channel Verification** | `.github/workflows/verify.yml` | `gh workflow run verify.yml` | Verifies binary installations in clean distro environments. |
| **C++ Linter** | `.github/workflows/cpp-linter.yml` | `gh workflow run cpp-linter.yml` | PR formatting and review annotations. |
| **Release Pipeline** | `.github/workflows/release.yml` | `mise run release <version>` (tags `v*`) | Builds multi-arch release assets and drafts GitHub Release. |
| **Nix Cache Sync** | `.github/workflows/nix-cache.yml` | `gh workflow run nix-cache.yml` | Rebuilds and pushes binaries to Cachix. |

### Monitoring Workflows via `gh` CLI
```bash
# Trigger and watch CI
gh workflow run ci.yml && gh run watch

# List recent workflow runs
gh run list --limit 5

# View failed logs for a specific run
gh run view <run_id> --log-failed
```

### Local Compilation (Incremental Dev only)
Use local builds exclusively for rapid C++ editing and local debugging:
```bash
# Configure debug preset (with address sanitizers / debug symbols)
mise run dev

# Incremental build
mise run build-debug

# Install locally to /usr for test
sudo mise run install

# Diagnostic health check (verifies service, binary paths, CMake cache)
mise run doctor

# Run clang-tidy static analysis
mise run tidy
```

---

### 一、GitHub Actions 编译优先原则与工作流

为了保证编译环境的纯净（依赖、Docker 隔离、Cachix 缓存）、避免本地机器过载以及各发行版交叉编译环境差异，制定了以下调用规范：

| 工作流名称 | 对应 Workflow 文件 | 触发方式 | 用途与说明 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CI 核心编译与测试** | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `gh workflow run ci.yml` | 完整的 C++ 构建、单元测试与依赖验证 |
| **全发行版打包流水线** | `.github/workflows/channels.yml` | `mise run channels` 或 `gh workflow run channels.yml` | 自动构建并打包 PPA、Fedora COPR、Flatpak、Debian |
| **安装验证测试** | `.github/workflows/verify.yml` | `gh workflow run verify.yml` | 在纯净各发行版容器中验证安装和启动 |
| **发布与制品流水线** | `.github/workflows/release.yml` | `mise run release <version>` (推送 `v*` tag) | 自动打包所有架构的 Release 制品并草拟 GitHub Release |
| **Nix 二进制缓存** | `.github/workflows/nix-cache.yml` | `gh workflow run nix-cache.yml` | 重新构建并推送到 Cachix 缓存 |

---

### 二、日常开发常用命令速查

```bash
# 1. 触发远程 CI 构建并实时观察日志
gh workflow run ci.yml && gh run watch

# 2. 触发多发行版打包
mise run channels

# 3. 检查最近运行的 Actions 状态
gh run list --limit 5

# 4. 查看最近失败步骤的具体错误日志
gh run view <run_id> --log-failed

# 5. 本地仅保留轻量增量调试 (不跑重型全量构建)
mise run dev          # 仅配置 debug 预设
mise run build-debug  # 仅做增量编译
```

---

### 三、更新的文件概览

1. **`AGENTS.md`**：新增第 3 节明确 **优先使用 GitHub Actions 编译**，并提供了 `gh workflow run` / `gh run watch` 的标准操作指令。

3. **`.agents/skills/vinput-dev/SKILL.md`**：在 Section 3 增加了完整的 Workflow 矩阵表、`gh` CLI 触发/监控 SOP，并明确本地与云端编译的边界分工。

## 3. Build & CI Workflows (Prioritize GitHub Actions)

### Core Principle: Prefer Remote GitHub Actions over Local Heavy Builds
To keep local machines clean, avoid toolchain drift, and leverage cloud caching (Cachix, ccache, multi-distro Docker runners), **always prioritize running compilation and package builds via GitHub Actions** rather than building heavy artifacts locally.

### GitHub Actions Workflows Reference

| Workflow | File | Trigger Command | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CI Build & Test** | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `gh workflow run ci.yml` | Standard build and test verification on Ubuntu runners. |
| **Packaging Channels** | `.github/workflows/channels.yml` | `mise run channels` or `gh workflow run channels.yml` | Builds across all distribution channels (PPA, COPR, Flatpak, Debian). |
| **Channel Verification** | `.github/workflows/verify.yml` | `gh workflow run verify.yml` | Verifies binary installations in clean distro environments. |
| **C++ Linter** | `.github/workflows/cpp-linter.yml` | `gh workflow run cpp-linter.yml` | PR formatting and review annotations. |
| **Release Pipeline** | `.github/workflows/release.yml` | `mise run release <version>` (tags `v*`) | Builds multi-arch release assets and drafts GitHub Release. |
| **Nix Cache Sync** | `.github/workflows/nix-cache.yml` | `gh workflow run nix-cache.yml` | Rebuilds and pushes binaries to Cachix. |

### Monitoring Workflows via `gh` CLI
```bash
# Trigger and watch CI
gh workflow run ci.yml && gh run watch

# List recent workflow runs
gh run list --limit 5

# View failed logs for a specific run
gh run view <run_id> --log-failed
```

Use local builds exclusively for rapid C++ editing and local debugging:
```bash

# Install locally to /usr for test

# Diagnostic health check (verifies service, binary paths, CMake cache)
mise run doctor

# Run clang-tidy static analysis

```
